implementation_statement: Group POL-02 Access Control Policy (P06) applies to the HCIS. The Hospital System supplement adds EHR break-glass, student and trainee, and clinical device account rules.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Employee and contractor EHR accounts are provisioned from SYS-G1 identity governance, driven by HR events, with role requests approved by unit managers. Gap: about 4,500 student and trainee accounts a year are created by the EHR security team from emailed rosters, outside identity governance and without end dates (group gap 4; POAM-001).
evidence: EV-006 (identity governance export); EV-041 (EHR user extract); EV-042 (student roster files)

implementation_statement: Provisioning, disabling, and quarterly certification campaigns for federated EHR accounts are automated in SYS-G1 identity governance.

control_name: Automated Temporary and Emergency Account Management
implementation_statement: Temporary accounts (agency nurses, locum physicians) expire automatically at the assignment end date entered by the staffing office; emergency accounts expire after 72 hours.
evidence: EV-006 (identity governance policy); EV-006 (agency account report)

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Federated accounts are disabled after 90 days of inactivity and on termination. Gap: local EHR accounts for students and trainees are not covered; 412 were active after their rotations ended (July 2026 sample; POAM-001).
evidence: EV-006 (inactivity job configuration); EV-C1-AC-2 (july 2026 student account sample)

implementation_statement: Account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal in SYS-G1 are logged and forwarded to the SIEM.

The SOC monitors sign-in anomalies from SYS-G1; the Hospital System Privacy Officer's team runs the EHR privacy monitoring tool for atypical record access (VIP, coworker, family, and same-surname rules) across all 9 hospitals.
evidence: EV-044 (privacy monitoring rules and weekly case log)

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The EHR enforces role-based security classes (about 1,900 templates mapped to job codes), department and hospital context, and sensitive-record flags (behavioral health, Part 2 records received from outside programs, employee-as-patient).
evidence: EV-041 (EHR security class matrix); EV-041 (sensitive-record configuration)

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The interface engine controls which messages flow to each partner (laboratory, health information exchange, public health, Health Plan admission notices). Gap: the admission-notice feed to the Health Plan sends full ADT segments rather than a minimum-necessary set (group gap 7; POAM-016).
evidence: EV-051 (interface route inventory); EV-051 (ADT feed specification)

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Separation of duties: EHR build analysts cannot promote their own changes to production; pharmacy formulary changes need a second pharmacist; security class changes need approval by the EHR security team lead.
evidence: EV-045 (change records); EV-041 (EHR security team procedure)

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Least privilege through job-code templates; access to other hospitals' patients is limited to roles with a cross-site need (transfer center, health information management, system pharmacists).
evidence: EV-041 (security class matrix); EV-041 (cross-site access review)

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Only the EHR security team can change security classes and user templates; the group identity team administers SYS-G1 roles.
Administrators use separate privileged accounts for server and database work; daily clinical work uses standard accounts.
Privileged access to EHR servers, databases, and the interface engine is granted just in time through PAM with approval and session recording.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Managers certify EHR access quarterly in identity governance; the EHR security team reviews privileged EHR security points twice a year.
Privileged sessions and EHR security point changes are logged and sent to the SIEM.
Accounts lock after 10 failed attempts for 15 minutes; badge-tap workstations lock the badge after 5 failed PIN attempts.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Clinical workstations lock after 10 minutes idle (2 minutes in public areas) and unlock with badge tap and PIN; downtime workstations lock after 5 minutes.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: EHR sessions end after 30 minutes of inactivity on shared workstations and 60 minutes on assigned workstations, per the Hospital System supplement.

Remote workforce access uses the group VPN or zero-trust access service with MFA. EHR and clinical application vendor support uses named accounts through PAM with session recording (medical device vendors are outside the HCIS boundary; see P04).
evidence: EV-005 (remote access configuration); EV-008 (vendor PAM account list)

control_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption
implementation_statement: Remote sessions use TLS 1.2 or higher.
Group POL-05 and the training standard apply.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Employees complete security and privacy training at hire and every year (98% completion) with monthly phishing exercises. Gap: the hospitals accept the schools' attestation for about 4,500 students and trainees and do not track their completion (POAM-003).
evidence: EV-027 (training completion report); EV-043 (school affiliation agreements)

implementation_statement: Annual training includes insider threat and privacy snooping cases from the EHR privacy monitoring program.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Role-based training: EHR training is required before account activation; downtime super users complete a downtime module each year; EHR security analysts complete security point training.
evidence: EV-027 (EHR training records); EV-048 (downtime super user roster)

implementation_statement: The group logging standard applies.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The EHR logs record access (view, print, export), orders, results, security point changes, and break-glass use; the ancillary systems log sign-ins and administrative changes.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: EHR audit records include user, patient, workstation, time, action, and department context.

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: The SOC reviews security events from the SIEM 24x7. The Privacy Officer's team reviews EHR privacy monitoring alerts weekly and investigates every VIP and employee-as-patient alert within 5 business days.
evidence: EV-011 (SOC case metrics); EV-044 (privacy case log)

implementation_statement: Review workflows are integrated in the SIEM case management system.
SYS-G1 sign-ins, EDR, firewall, and EHR application logs are correlated in the SIEM.
SIEM storage is write-once and administered only by the SOC platform team.
Security logs are kept 1 year online and 6 years archived; EHR access logs are kept 7 years in the EHR.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Audit generation is enabled for all EHR modules and the ancillary systems in the boundary.
Group assessment and authorization procedures apply.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Group internal audit assesses the common controls once a year and sampled HCIS controls (P07, 2026-07-06 to 2026-08-28). The Hospital System security and compliance lead assesses the remaining HCIS controls on a 3-year cycle.
Group internal audit reports to the board audit committee and neither designs nor operates the controls it assesses.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Interconnection agreements exist for external partners (reference laboratory, health information exchange, public health). Gap: the routine feeds to the Health Plan run under the intercompany data sharing addendum without a written minimum-necessary protocol (POAM-016).

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Findings go to the group POA&M (P07) with owners and dates; the Hospital System lead reports status monthly.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Internal authorization decision by the Group CISO and the Group Chief Risk Officer, with conditions (section 4.2).

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Continuous monitoring through SIEM dashboards, vulnerability scans, access certifications, and quarterly control metrics to the Hospital System risk committee.
An external firm penetration-tests the data centers and the EHR web services each year (last test 2026-03).
Group configuration management standard applies.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Baselines exist for EHR application servers, database servers, clinical workstations, and downtime workstations.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The EHR change control board approves all build, upgrade, and interface changes; emergency changes are reviewed the next business day.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Each change includes a clinical safety and security impact review; medication and order-set changes require pharmacy and nursing informatics sign-off.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Only the release team can promote to production; access is through PAM.
Server and workstation hardening settings are enforced by group configuration management and checked weekly.
Application allow-listing on downtime workstations; unused services disabled on servers per baseline.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The HCIS inventory lists servers, databases, interfaces, and workstations. Gap: medical devices and analyzers that send data into the HCIS through the interface engine are not linked to their interfaces in the inventory (POAM-011).
Group POL-03 and the group continuity standard apply, together with the unified emergency preparedness program.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The HCIS contingency plan covers site loss with failover to DC2 and clinical downtime procedures. Gaps: it assumes DC2 is clean, so it has no strategy for ransomware that reaches both data centers; it is not tied to the emergency plan's diversion and transfer procedures; downtime workstations at 3 community hospitals were not tested in the last 12 months (POAM-009, POAM-012).
evidence: EV-046 (HCIS contingency plan v4 (2025)); EV-048 (downtime test log)

implementation_statement: Coordination with the unified emergency preparedness plan is informal; the emergency plan's risk assessment has no system-wide IT outage scenario (POAM-023).
Downtime super users on every unit complete annual downtime training; ED and pharmacy staff drill paper workflows each year.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The DC2 failover is tested every year (2026 test: EHR back in 1 hour 40 minutes). Gap: no test of a restore from the immutable vault, so the 5- to 7-day rebuild estimate is unverified (POAM-012).

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud platform and backup vault
implementation_statement: Backups are copied daily to the immutable vault at cloud provider B, in a separate account with a separate backup identity.
DC2 is the alternate processing site, about 300 miles from DC1, with capacity for the full EHR and ancillary systems. It shares the directory forest with DC1 (see CP-10).
Each hospital has diverse WAN carriers; EDs and command centers have analog lines and EMS radios.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud platform and backup vault
implementation_statement: Daily backups of EHR databases, ancillary systems, and configuration; storage snapshots every 15 minutes in DC1 and DC2.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud platform and backup vault
implementation_statement: Backup integrity is checked automatically; sample file restores are tested each month.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Recovery to DC2 is documented and tested. Gap: reconstitution after a compromise that reaches both data centers has no clean recovery environment and no tested sequence (POAM-012).
Group identification and authentication standard applies.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Every employee, contractor, student, and trainee has a unique EHR account. Federated users sign in through SYS-G1; students and trainees use local EHR accounts (POAM-001).
Privileged access requires phishing-resistant MFA through PAM.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Workforce users unlock clinical workstations with badge tap and PIN (two factors) and use MFA for remote access and email. Gap: students and trainees sign in to the EHR with a password only (POAM-001).
Identifiers are issued from HR records and never reused.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Workforce authenticators follow group rules. Gap: 63 interface and service accounts used by the interface engine and ancillary systems have static passwords older than 1 year (POAM-002).
Passwords: at least 14 characters, checked against breached-password lists.
Users at the 64 community-connect practices sign in through the practices' own identity providers federated to SYS-H1, with MFA required by contract; patients use the portal's own identity service.
Group POL-03 applies.
SOC analysts and division incident liaisons train each year; hospital incident command staff train on the cyber annex.
Technical playbooks are tested each quarter. Gap: no cross-division exercise of the notification matrix or the ransomware downtime and diversion runbook (POAM-005).
24x7 incident handling by the group SOC with playbooks; Hospital System liaison on every Severity 1 or 2 bridge.
Incidents are tracked in the SIEM case system with discovery dates recorded for each covered entity.
Staff report to the SOC within 1 hour. Gap: the external notification matrix does not yet include all College and state insurance contacts and has not been exercised (POAM-005).
Group incident response plan v5 (2025). Gap: it does not cover the College or link to the emergency preparedness program's incident command and diversion steps (POAM-005).
Nonlocal maintenance of HCIS servers and applications uses vendor accounts in PAM with approval per session and recording.
Data center media are sanitized or destroyed with certificates; workstation drives are wiped before reuse.
Data center access lists are approved by the infrastructure director and reviewed each quarter.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Data centers use badge and biometric entry with escorts; hospital server and network closets use badge access managed by hospital security.
Group planning policy applies.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: This SSP; reviewed each year and after major changes.
Workforce acknowledges POL-05 and the Hospital System supplement at hire and each year; students sign the rules of behavior at rotation start.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: HCIS architecture places EHR web, application, and database tiers in separate zones in each data center.
Group information security program plan (POL-01).
The Group CISO leads the program; the Hospital System security and compliance lead is the hospital covered entity's Security Official.
Group risk management strategy and acceptance levels (POL-01 4.4).
Group personnel security procedures apply.
Background checks for employees before hire; licensure verification for clinical staff.
HR termination events disable SYS-G1 accounts within 4 hours (immediately for involuntary terminations).

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Staffing agencies and locum firms must report end dates under contract. Gap: affiliation agreements with 22 outside schools do not require them to report early withdrawals or rotation changes (POAM-014).
Sanctions applied and documented by HR with the Privacy Officer.

control_name: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information
implementation_statement: The Notice of Privacy Practices and the Privacy Rule define the authority to use and disclose PHI in the HCIS.

Purposes are documented for treatment, payment, and operations uses. Gap: the purposes and data elements for routine disclosures to the Health Plan are not documented in a minimum-necessary protocol (group gap 7; POAM-016).
Group risk assessment policy applies.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Security categorization in section 6 of this plan.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: The 2026 risk analysis (P01) covers the HCIS and rolls up to the group register.
Supply chain risk assessments for tier 1 clinical vendors (EHR, laboratory, imaging, pharmacy automation).
Authenticated scans of HCIS servers every week; critical findings fixed within 15 days (but see SI-2 for ancillary servers).

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Risk responses recorded in the registers and the POA&M.

responsible_role: Hospital System security and compliance lead
implementation_statement: Criticality analysis from the BIA (P05): the EHR, laboratory, pharmacy, and imaging components are mission-critical.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Clinical system contracts include BAAs, security requirements, vulnerability notification, and support-life commitments.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Security engineering principles applied in the EHR architecture (tiering, least privilege, defense in depth).
External services (EHR vendor support, reference laboratory, health information exchange) have BAAs and annual assurance reviews.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: The EHR vendor's release and configuration management is reviewed through its SOC 2 report and release notes; local build is version-controlled.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Unsupported components are tracked. Gap: 11 ancillary servers (analyzer middleware, two pharmacy automation servers) run an unsupported operating system pending vendor upgrades; they sit in restricted zones (POAM-010).

External boundaries use next-generation firewalls with deny-by-default rules. Gap: inside the data centers, Health Plan, College file share, and HCIS server zones are not separated from each other at the network or directory level (POAM-007).

control_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception
implementation_statement: External boundary rules deny by default and allow by exception.
ePHI in transit is protected with TLS across the WAN and to partners.
Cryptographic protection: TLS 1.2 or higher; HL7 interfaces over VPN or TLS.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud platform and backup vault
implementation_statement: Keys for database and backup encryption are managed in group key management with rotation each year.

provider_if_inherited: SYS-G3 Group cloud platform and backup vault
implementation_statement: Validated cryptographic modules for storage and transport encryption.
EHR and ancillary databases and storage are encrypted at rest; downtime workstations use full-disk encryption.
Cryptographic protection of data at rest with group-managed keys.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: Operating system patches are applied monthly. Gap: ancillary clinical servers wait for vendor validation; median time to apply critical patches is 47 days against a 30-day target (POAM-010).
EDR on all HCIS servers and workstations, including downtime workstations.
24x7 monitoring of HCIS servers, the EHR web tier, and privileged sessions.

control_name: Automated Tools and Mechanisms for Real-time Analysis
implementation_statement: Automated real-time analysis and alerting in the SIEM.
Inbound and outbound traffic at the data center edge is monitored, including unusual outbound volume.

responsible_role: HCIS system owner (Hospital System clinical applications director)
implementation_statement: File integrity monitoring on EHR application servers; pharmacy formulary and drug library changes are logged and reviewed by a second pharmacist.
evidence: EV-045 (integrity monitoring configuration); EV-045 (formulary change log)

implementation_statement: Group retention schedule; medical record retention per state law (each state where the hospitals operate).
Group supply chain risk management plan covers clinical software and device vendors.
Tier 1 clinical vendors are reviewed each year (SOC 2 reports, questionnaires).
